_comment: Shahnama of Firdausi, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. II: Sohrab's march, White Castle, Gurdafrid. Paraphrase passages with notes.

title.en: Sohrab Chooses His Charger and Marches on Iran

region.zh: 薩曼甘馬群（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. II, Suhrab secs. 5-7

summary.en: Sohrab demands a charger swift of foot with hoofs of steel flint-shattering; his might breaks down many a noble steed until a warrior brings a colt of the breed of Rakhsh, in strength a lion and as fleet as wind, whose leap is like the lightning. Mounted, Sohrab appears like Mount Bisitun, his spear pillar-like, and asks his grandsire's leave to seek Iran and see his glorious sire. Afrasiyab, delighted, sends Barman and Human with twelve thousand troops and a secret policy: the father must not recognise his son, that matchless Rustam may be slain — and should the boy perish by his father's hand, that hero's heart will never cease to burn.
summary.zh: 蘇赫拉布索求鋼蹄碎石、疾如飛鳥的戰馬；他的神力折服諸多駿馬，直到有人獻上「拉赫什血統」的雄駒——力如獅、疾如風、躍如閃電。少年上馬如比斯通山聳立，向祖父請命赴伊朗「拜見生父」。阿弗拉西亞卜大喜，遣巴爾曼與胡曼率一萬二千人並授密計：務使父子互不相認，讓無敵的魯斯塔姆隕落；若少年死於父親之手，那位英雄之心將永燃悔恨之火。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; Afrasiyab's intrigue is the tragic engine of the Sohrab story. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Thou shalt see my prowess, said Sohrab, but I must have a charger swift of foot with hoofs of steel flint-shattering, in strength like elephants, in flight like birds, in water like fish, and on the land like deer. His mother bade the herdsman bring his herds of horses for Sohrab to choose a charger; and when some large-limbed, lusty steed appeared Sohrab flung round its neck the leathern noose, then laid his hand upon the beast to prove it and made it grovel. Thus his might broke down full many a noble steed.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Suhrab sec. 6 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: At length a warrior approached the elephantine youth and said: I have a colt, one of the breed of Rakhsh, in strength a lion and as fleet as wind; beneath the stamping of his hoofs the Bull-fish quaketh; his leap is like the lightning; on the mountains he goeth like the raven, on the water like fish, upon the desert like shaft from bow. Sohrab laughed out for joy, both proved and approved it, saddled and mounted; he appeared like Mount Bisitun, his spear was pillar-like. Since I have gotten such a steed I must ride forth at once and turn the day of Kai Kaus to gloom.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Suhrab sec. 6 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Afrasiyab had news: Suhrab hath launched his ship, a host hath gathered unto him; although his mouth still savoureth of milk his mind is set on shaft and scimitar. He chose two chiefs, Human and Barman, gave them twelve thousand valiant troops and said: be this your secret policy: the father must not recognise his son by any ties of instinct, love, or race; so, when the twain encounter, the matchless Rustam will be put to it; it may be that this lion-man will slay him. Then will we press Kaus and seize on Iran with Rustam gone; while should he perish by his father's hand, that hero's heart will never cease to burn.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Suhrab sec. 7 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

title.zh: 古爾達弗里德城堡前現真容

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. II, Suhrab secs. 8-11

summary.en: At White Castle veteran Hajir rides out against the boy and is thrown like a boulder to the earth; his daughter Gurdafrid, a woman ever famous in the fight, arms herself, conceals her tresses under her mail, and showers arrows on Sohrab, who abashed charges, rents her mail with a dart, and snatches off her helm — her hair escapes, her face shines like the sun: it is a girl! He lassoes her round the waist, but she bargains: chiefs should be wise, so let us keep it dark; our troops and stronghold are at thy command. Then from the ramparts she mocks him: when news shall reach the Shah, he will march forth with Rustam whom ye cannot stand against; woe is me that such a neck and shoulder should disappear within the maw of pards.
summary.zh: 白堡守將海吉爾出戰，竟被少年如巨石般摔落於地。其女古爾達弗里德——征戰聞名的巾幗英雄——披甲藏髮出戰，箭如飛蝗；蘇赫拉布慚愧而奮擊，一鏢撕裂其鎧甲，奪其盔——長髮飄散、面容如日：「原來是女子！」他以套索擒其腰；她卻與之講和：「智者不逞匹夫之勇，堡壘兵馬任憑差遣。」隨後在城頭譏笑他：等卡烏斯與魯斯塔姆大軍一到，你這等英偉的脖頸怕要葬身獅腹！

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; Gurdafrid's taunt plants the fatal ambiguity of Sohrab's identity. No living community restriction.

passages.text: White Castle was a stronghold of Iran and veteran Hajir was castellan, a man of might and courage; for Gazhdaham was failing though still brave and venturesome. His daughter, who was proud, renowned, and malapert, bore arms and fought on horseback. As Sohrab approached, Hajir sped forth upon the field. Suhrab rushed from the host as 'twere a blast: what are thy name and lineage? She that bare will have to weep for thee.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Suhrab sec. 8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Hajir laughed out and charged; brave Sohrab, strong as an elephant, came on like fire upon his moving mountain of a steed. Hajir thrust at his waist; the spearpoint glanced. Sohrab struck with the butt his foe's waist lustily and threw him like a boulder to the earth, astound in heart and soul. Suhrab dismounted, sat on his foeman's breast; Hajir entreated quarter, was made fast in bonds, and sent to Human.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Suhrab sec. 8 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: A woman like some valiant cavalier was she and ever famous in the fight; her name was Gurdafrid, and none as yet had seen her match. Time pressed, she armed, concealed her tresses underneath her mail, secured her Ruman casque upon her head, and came down, like a lion, from the hold with girded waist upon a wind-foot steed. What lusty Crocodile is there among you to match himself with me in single combat? she cried in thunder-tones.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Suhrab sec. 9 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: He thrust a deadly dart with all his strength, struck Gurdafrid upon the belt and rent her coat of mail, but even as she reeled she drew her sword and clave the dart asunder; he pressed upon her, jostled her, and snatched her helm: her hair escaped, her face shone like the sun. It is a girl! he said amazed. He caught her round the waist, but she showed her face and said: chiefs should be wise, so let us keep it dark; our troops and stronghold are at thy command. Then, laughing, from the ramparts she mocked him: when news shall reach the Shah that a chief is leading an army from Turan, he will march forth with Rustam whom ye cannot stand against, and all thy host will perish; woe is me that such a neck and shoulder should disappear within the maw of pards.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Suhrab secs. 9-11 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
